symptom: A nested `Body: MAPPING` on a consumed REST operation makes the project **impossible to open** — mxbuild throws `System.AggregateException … (Export Object Mappings cannot have ObjectHandling set to 'Create')` instead of reporting an error
cause: The inline serializer passed the literal `"Create"` for every nested child regardless of namespace, so an EXPORT object element got an illegal handling. This is not a check error: it is thrown while **loading** the model, before any check runs, so `mx check` cannot even reach the project — and `mxcli check` and `exec` both accept it
insight: Nested export elements are `Find` with backup `Error`, which is what Studio Pro stores on an export mapping DOCUMENT — there is no inline export body anywhere in the demo corpus to pin against (**0** `Rest$ImplicitMappingBody` across 9 packages), so the document form is the reference and mxbuild loading the project is the control. Keep a control test for the IMPORT direction in the same file: nested import elements legitimately stay `Create`, and a fix that flips both is wrong. Note the asymmetry when reproducing: a build error you can see is a *better* failure than this one — always confirm the project LOADS, not just that the check is green. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/rest-inline-mapping-paths.mdl`, test `TestInlineExportBodyNestedHandling`. mxcli-rest FINDINGS #37
